title: Tiered conditional approval flow and pricebook convergence for special-term enterprise deals
creator: Priya Menon
description: Problem: Sales and RevOps manually review and approve discounts for enterprise deals tied to security questionnaire (SQ) exceptions. This creates delays, inconsistent outcomes, and manual pricebook edits that sometimes drift from the canonical product pricebook. Goal: Build a tiered, rules-driven approval flow that programmatically enforces discount guardrails, surfaces SQ gating earlier, and automates two-way sync with the canonical pricebook to reduce manual edits by 80% and approval latency by 60% for affected deals. Scope: - Define discount tiers and conditional approvers that incorporate SQ risk flags - Implement a deterministic approval routing service in RevOps stack (ENG) - Add telemetry to measure decisioning, overrides, and time-to-approval - Build a pricebook converger job that reconciles negotiated terms back into pricebook drafts and produces audit-ready artifacts - UX: Add an approvals panel in the internal deal desk UI and notification hooks to Slack/Email Out of scope: External quoting tool integration (manual mapping will be handled in a follow-up), automated legal clause drafting.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic approval routing engine exists and routes discounts to the correct approver according to rules (tier, SQ risk)
Pricebook converger runs nightly and flags divergent entries with root-cause notes visible in the admin UI
Telemetry dashboard tracks per-deal time-to-approval, override rate, and SQ-triggered escalation incidents
Approval overrides require mandatory justification and create an immutable audit entry linked to the deal and SQ artifacts
Rollout plan and runbook exist for a phased pilot with two enterprise accounts and RevOps team sign-off
